>
[Spirit-Singer](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4242)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Etheric spirit-singers create an eerie spectral sound based on the presence of spiritual essence and other ethereal energies. All spirit-singers can be used as musical instruments by manipulating the sensitivity to ethereal energies. However, they have an even greater benefit in areas heavy with spiritual essence. When played in the presence of a significant spiritual disturbance, such as a haunt or an incorporeal undead, a spirit‑singer grants you a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks. While playing a spirit-singer, you also gain a +1 item bonus to checks to detect a [haunt](/Traits.aspx?ID=622) or [incorporeal ](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722), and you can roll a check to notice a haunt even if you aren’t actively Searching for it, due to the distortions of the spirit-singer’s music. A haunt or incorporeal undead that is intelligent enough to notice the effects it is having on the spirit-singer’s music and that can’t otherwise communicate with the living might choose to use the spirit-singer to do so if it wishes. For instance, it could try to guide the spirit-singer player towards a location by creating distortions in that direction or, if it understands language, it could try to answer questions by creating one distortion for yes and two distortions for no. Unless stated otherwise in its usage entry, a spirit-singer functions like a heavy musical instrument; rather than carrying it, the musician places the spirit‑singer in a particular position and uses both hands to play.

    level="1"
    right="Item 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spiritsight Ring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2346)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 154, [Pathfinder #176: Lost Mammoth Valley](/Sources.aspx?ID=113) pg. 81

**Price** 225 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The opal set in the intricately carved ivory _spiritsight ring_ eventually becomes translucent and tickles your finger whenever an [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creature is nearby. When in the presence of a nearby incorporeal creature, even if it's within a solid object, you eventually detect the creature, though you might not do so instantly, and you can't pinpoint the location. This acts as a [vague sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=413), like humans' sense of smell. An incorporeal creature trying to hide its presence from this sense attempts a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check against your Perception DC to hide from your vague sense, as normal for attempting to foil [special senses](/Rules.aspx?ID=414). You gain a +2 item bonus when using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) action to find [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) incorporeal creatures within 30 feet of you.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

_Spiritsight tea_ exudes a soft blue glow, creating illumination equal to that of a candle. When consumed, your eyes take on a soft glow as well, and you can see invisible creatures and objects for 10 minutes; such creatures appear to you as translucent shapes, and they're [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) to you. You gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) creatures. 

---

 [Tea Ceremony](/Traits.aspx?ID=738) The duration of being able to see invisible creatures and objects increases to 30 minutes, and the duration of the item bonus increases to 8 hours.

May contain spoilers from Blood Lords **Source** [Pathfinder #185: A Taste of Ashes](/Sources.aspx?ID=188) pg. 78 **Price** 1,600 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands or mounted **Bulk** 3 --- This drum-shaped metal floodlight has a metal handle on each side and a housing at its base to be slotted into a stand or pedestal. A _splendid floodlight_ has a primary function as well as several secondary functions available by rotating through a series of translucent sheets called gels. A _splendid floodlight_ comes with the four gels described below, but other gels exist with different abilities. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per hour; **Requirements** The _splendid floodlight's_ light is off; **Effect** You flip a switch and the _splendid floodlight_ emits bright magical light in a 120-foot cone that hangs in the air and remains in place even if you move the floodlight. If the cone passes through an area of magical [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) or targets a creature affected by magical darkness, the splendid floodlight attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the darkness. Creatures in the cone who are [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) reduce the value of their frightened condition by 1 at the beginning of each turn they start in the area of the cone. The light remains in place until you Interact to flip the switch again to extinguish the floodlight. If you haven't done so after an hour, the switch flips on its own and the floodlight turns off. **Activate** Interact; **Requirements** The _splendid floodlight's_ light is on; **Effect** You rotate one of the following gels into position in the floodlight or rotate a gel out. You can do this even if the _splendid floodlight_ has been moved from its position when the light was created. You can have up to two gels in place at once; if you rotate in a third, another of your choice rotates out.
  • **Red Gel** The light lends an air of gravitas to all creatures illuminated by it. Creatures in the light gain a +2 item bonus to Charisma-based skill checks.
  • **Yellow Gel** [Invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) creatures and objects are visible while in the light, and creatures with the [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=149) trait appear substantial rather than ghostly.
  • **Green Gel** All creatures illuminated by the light appear to be wearing exceptionally stylish clothing with elegantly coiffed hair styles.
  • **Blue Gel** [Undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creatures in the light appear as they did when alive, and living creatures in the light appear decayed, like an undead creature.

>
[Sprite Apple](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1932)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 51

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>1 minute ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A sparkling candy coating covers a sprite apple. For 10 minutes after consuming a sprite apple, you shed [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot emanation (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 20 feet). While shedding this light, you can't be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) if you're visible, and if you're [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), you're concealed instead rather than being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39). The light matches the vibrant color of the apple's candy coating. Creatures in the bright light are subject to another effect, depending on the type of apple.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 5"
pfs="Standard"
>
Sprite Apple (Chartreuse)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 51

**Price** 26 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Creatures in the bright light feel more in tune with nature, gaining a +1 item bonus to Nature checks and to Diplomacy checks attempted against animals or plants (if they have the [Animal Empathy](/Feats.aspx?ID=4709) feat, [Plant Empathy](/Feats.aspx?ID=4711) feat, or some other ability to make such checks).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Sprite Apple (Golden)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 51

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Creatures in the bright light feel kind and inviting, taking a –1 item penalty to their Will DC against [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Sprite Apple (Pink)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 51

**Price** 16 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Creatures in the bright light feel a burst of creativity, gaining a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 6"
pfs="Standard"
>
Sprite Apple (Teal)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 51

**Price** 41 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

Creatures in the bright light feel a sense of calm, gaining a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68) effects.

For 10 minutes after consuming a sprite apple, you shed bright light in a 20-foot emanation (and dim light for the next 20 feet). A sparkling candy coating covers a sprite apple. For 10 minutes after consuming a sprite apple, you shed [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) in a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) for the next 20 feet). While shedding this light, you can’t be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) if you’re visible, and if you’re [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83), you’re concealed instead rather than being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96). The light matches the vibrant color of the apple’s candy coating. Creatures in the bright light are subject to another effect, depending on the type of apple.

>
[Stag's Helm](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1752)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 589

**Price** 240 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This impressive-looking helmet is crafted to resemble the skull of a mighty stag. Although made from bone, the antlers and helm are as strong as iron. While the Stag Lord himself wears this helmet in the Kingmaker Adventure Path, _stag's helms_ are actually the creation of the church of [Erastil](/Deities.aspx?ID=6), and worshipers of this deity find that the helm is not only particularly comfortable to wear, but that they can activate it once per hour rather than once per day.

 Rather than restrict the senses, a _stag's helm_ enhances them, causing the world to appear in more vibrant colors and significantly enhancing the ambient sounds of the region without making them distracting. While worn, it grants a +1 item bonus to Perception checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" />  ;  **Frequency** once per day (or once per hour if the wearer worships Erastil);   **Effect** Choose a single creature within 30 feet. The _stag's helm_ focuses your aim and grants supernatural insight into your next shot. Your target is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) to the next ranged Strike you make this turn against them.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 13"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Stage Magician's Cloak](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3634)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Curtain Call</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 81

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This black velvet cloak has a silvery blue iridescent lining. The cloak can be worn with either side facing out—switching from one side to the other requires two Interact actions. If these actions are both taken on the same turn, the act of removing and redonning the cloak doesn’t cause it to lose its [investiture](/Rules.aspx?ID=3163). When worn with the black velvet lining facing out, the _stage magician’s cloak_ grants a +2 item bonus to [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) checks. When worn with the silvery blue lining facing out, it grants a +2 item bonus to [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) checks. 

**Activate—Now You See Me...** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Distracting colorful smoke blasts outward from the cloak in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387), causing all creatures in the area to become [off‑guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of your next turn (DC 30 Will save). If you were previously [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79), or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96), you lose those conditions. You become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 round and may use the extra action to [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297), [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306), or [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305).

**Activate—...Now You Don't** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Harmless silver smoke issues from the cloak in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). You cast a 2nd-rank [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1577) on yourself and are transported, along with all items you’re wearing and holding, from your current space to an unoccupied space within 30 feet that you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you’re carrying it in an extradimensional space—the transportation part of this effect fails.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 13 Stage Magician's Cloak May contain spoilers from Curtain Call Unique Invested Magical Source Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright pg. 81 Price 3,000 gp Usage worn cloak Bulk L This black velvet cloak has a silvery blue iridescent lining. The cloak can be worn with either side facing out—switching from one side to the other requires two Interact actions. If these actions are both taken on the same turn, the act of removing and redonning the cloak doesn’t cause it to lose its investiture. When worn with the black velvet lining facing out, the stage magician’s cloak grants a +2 item bonus to Occultism checks. When worn with the silvery blue lining facing out, it grants a +2 item bonus to Arcana checks. Activate—Now You See Me... Two Actions (manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect Distracting colorful smoke blasts outward from the cloak in a 10-foot emanation, causing all creatures in the area to become off‑guard until the start of your next turn (DC 30 Will save). If you were previously concealed, hidden, or undetected, you lose those conditions. You become quickened for 1 round and may use the extra action to Interact, Strike, or Stride. Activate—...Now You Don't Two Actions (manipulate, teleportation) Frequency once per day; Effect Harmless silver smoke issues from the cloak in a 10-foot emanation. You cast a 2nd-rank invisibility on yourself and are transported, along with all items you’re wearing and holding, from your current space to an unoccupied space within 30 feet that you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you’re carrying it in an extradimensional space—the transportation part of this effect fails.

[Stalk Goggles](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1821)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Morph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=113" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #187: The Seventh Arch](/Sources.aspx?ID=192) pg. 80

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These black leather goggle frames have no lenses. Instead, when a character puts them on and invests them, the wearer's eyes transform and lengthen into snail-like eyestalks. The wobbly eyestalks stretch out through the lens holes and up over the wearer's head on lengthened optic nerves.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** By focusing hard, you can watch for enemies in all directions. You gain [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=1) for 1 minute; during this time, you can't be flanked.

>
[Stampede Medallion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1080)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Eidolon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=386" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 190

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you invest this medallion for your eidolon, it changes shape to appear as a tiny bejeweled facsimile of the eidolon, magically attached just over your eidolon's heart. While your eidolon wears the medallion, they gain a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon Concentrates on the medallion and their connection to you, allowing them to momentarily manifest into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an emanation around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon's Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared.

**Activate—Impossible Tide** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon momentarily manifests into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon’s Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared.

---

Astrolabes can be used for navigation in unfamiliar or featureless locations. To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49). By spending 1 minute to measure the height of the stars and planets, a holder who knows the time and date can determine the latitude, and a holder who knows their latitude can determine the date and time. An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies. A standard astrolabe functions only on steady ground.

These standards are always constructed from uncut wood and a leather banner painted with the visage of a snarling beast—a wolf, boar, bear, lion, dragon, or similarly imposing creature. And while it might become lost on a battlefield scattered with gaudier standards, its effect bolsters those around a competent leader. When carrying this banner, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks and initiative rolls, and creatures in a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) also gain a +1 item bonus to initiative checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** An ally within 20 feet of you critically hits with a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306); **Requirements** You have the [Battle Cry](/Feats.aspx?ID=5124) skill feat; **Effect** You attempt to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) the foe the Strike hit.

fields.item_bonus_note: Astronomy Lore
fields.markdown:
May contain spoilers from Malevolence **Source** [Malevolence](/Sources.aspx?ID=88) pg. 67 **Price** 650 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Even during the time of Thassilon, when the Order of the Starless Night still existed, _starless scopes_ were uncommon. Today, this final scope might well be the last one to survive the passage of time. A _starless scope_ is a handheld telescope crafted of silver and fine wood. When one peers at the sky through a _starless scope_, one always views the sky as if during a clear night. A starless scope adds a +2 item bonus to [Astronomy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) and Perception checks made to observe the skies, as it causes all celestial objects to dim when not directly observed, allowing its user to more easily observe their intended subject. It also grants a +2 item bonus to all [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks made to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24). A starless scope also functions as a divine focus for worshipers of [Desna](/Deities.aspx?ID=5). The magic of a starless scope requires a specially prepared lens to function, and it's possible to shatter the lens if you roll poorly when activating the _starless scope_. Without a functional lens, a _starless scope_ doesn't function. You can replace a shattered lens with a functional lens by taking a two-action activity with the manipulate trait. If you know the formula for the starless scope, you can [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) a new lens with a DC 25 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) (master) check. A starless scope lens is a level 9 item worth 100 gp. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** you use the _starless scope_ as a divine focus; **Requirements** you worship Desna; **Effect** You attempt to enhance the effects of a spell as you cast it by attempting a [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) check against the spell's DC, as determined by [Table 10–5](/Rules.aspx?ID=554) **Critical Success** Any attack rolls you make with the spell gain a +2 status bonus, and any saving throw a foe makes against the spell takes a –2 status penalty. If you would normally cast the spell from a spell slot, and the spell is 5th level or lower, you don't spend the spell slot and cast the spell from the _starless scope_ instead.
**Success** Any attack rolls you make with the spell gain a +1 status bonus, and any saving throw a foe makes against the spell takes a –1 status penalty.
**Failure** The spell is cast normally. Attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a failure, the _starless scope's_ lens shatters.
**Critical Failure** The spell is disrupted and the _starless scope's_ lens shatters. **Activate** Interact ([abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You raise the scope to your eye and observe a creature within 30 feet. You can attempt to identify the creature by [Recalling Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). The _starless scope_ adds a +2 item bonus to this check. If the creature is associated with the Dominion of the Black or the Elder Mythos, or is a creature whose actions have blasphemed against Desna (Ioseff Xarwin's ghost falls into this latter category), the creature must attempt a DC 27 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected, and the _starless scope's_ lens shatters.
**Success** The creature shines with starlight for 1 round. During this time, the creature can't be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) if it is visible. If it's [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), it's concealed rather than being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39). The creature takes a –1 status penalty to saving throws against [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) effects while it shimmers with starlight.
**Failure** As success, but the creature also suffers an additional effect. An [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creature loses its incorporeal trait as long as it shines with starlight. Any other creature becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) as long as it shines with starlight.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the duration of the starlight is 1 minute, and the status penalty to saving throws against divine effects increases to –2.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #152: Legacy of the Lost God](/Sources.aspx?ID=23) pg. 75

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Woven from swaths of rich brocade silk and embroidered with ancient Azlanti script in golden thread, this stole imparts a noble appearance to even the homeliest of individuals when draped over the shoulders. While wearing a stole of civility, you receive a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) with humans or [Make a Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) of humans, and a +2 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks against humans. The stole also grants you full understanding of the [Azlanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=49) language.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** you are a human; **Effect** You gain 10 temporary Hit Points, which last for 10 minutes.

>
[Stone of Encouragement](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2467)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 87

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Second-mark members of the Firebrands have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This smooth, round, gray stone fits neatly into the palm of your hand and feels comfortable to hold regardless of the size or shape of your hand. While you're holding the stone, it telepathically speaks to you at regular intervals in generic words of encouragement, such as “You can do it!” and “Let's go!” The encouraging words manifest in the voice of your internal monologue or take on the characteristics of the voice of someone you trust. Despite the similarity, you're aware that the stone is telepathically projecting its voice and can differentiate between the stone's voice and your internal monologue or the voice of the person you trust.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You ask the stone for help with a task. It speaks a few motivating words related to the task at hand, which grants you a +1 item bonus to the first skill check you attempt within 1 minute. You become temporarily immune to the effects of all _stones of encouragement_, even ones other than the one you activated, for 1 day. You can still hear the encouraging words of different stones if you hold them, but they don't provide any benefits.

fields.text: Item 2+ Stone of Encouragement Uncommon Divination Magical Source Firebrands pg. 87 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Access Second-mark members of the Firebrands have access to this item. This smooth, round, gray stone fits neatly into the palm of your hand and feels comfortable to hold regardless of the size or shape of your hand. While you're holding the stone, it telepathically speaks to you at regular intervals in generic words of encouragement, such as “You can do it!” and “Let's go!” The encouraging words manifest in the voice of your internal monologue or take on the characteristics of the voice of someone you trust. Despite the similarity, you're aware that the stone is telepathically projecting its voice and can differentiate between the stone's voice and your internal monologue or the voice of the person you trust. Activate Single Action command; Frequency once per day; Effect You ask the stone for help with a task. It speaks a few motivating words related to the task at hand, which grants you a +1 item bonus to the first skill check you attempt within 1 minute. You become temporarily immune to the effects of all stones of encouragement , even ones other than the one you activated, for 1 day. You can still hear the encouraging words of different stones if you hold them, but they don't provide any benefits. Item 2 Stone of Encouragement Source Firebrands pg. 87 Price 30 gp Bulk L Item 8 Stone of Encouragement (Greater) Source Firebrands pg. 87 Price 475 gp Bulk L The item bonus is +2.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Triumph of the Tusk</spoilers>

<traits>

<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #207: Resurrection Flood](/Sources.aspx?ID=249) pg. 80

**Price** 45 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

Your skin becomes a canvas that records history as you learn it. When you receive the tattoo, choose a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill. You can add the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait to the [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) action in order to study your tattoos, granting you a +1 item bonus to your check using the chosen Lore skill. A storied skin tattoo starts with an icon that represents a central event in your subject of study and is usually placed on the forehead or over the heart. Each time you learn about a major event in the history of that subject, an image, design, or symbol appears on your skin to represent the event.

**Activate—Living History** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** The tattoo’s design animates for 1 round, crudely portraying some scene associated with the chosen Lore skill.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #208: Hoof, Cinder, and Storm](/Sources.aspx?ID=250) pg. 78

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These shards of coalesced necromantic essence are sometimes found in the wake of an ancestor storm. Howling spirits are faintly visible, trapped inside the jagged, dark-green glass.

You can use the shard to cow the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) or briefly release the tormented souls from inside the glass. While you hold the stormshard, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks to [influence](/Rules.aspx?ID=1830) the undead. In addition, you can [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) undead creatures, even if those creatures are [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) or otherwise [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2313) to [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), or [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects.

**Activate—Free the Spirits** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You briefly release the spirits from the _stormshard_ before drawing them back into the glass. Each creature in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) takes 4d8 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2247) Fortitude save). You treat the result of your saving throw as one degree of success better than its outcome.

This _[+1 ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2785) [explorer’s clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=39)_ is a simple, practical, and unassuming two-piece outfit. The comfortable fabric is enchanted with illusory magic to make it look as if the wearer is wearing heavy armor (as _[_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568)_). While wearing the suit, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) someone who would normally wear heavy armor. 

**Activate—Faux Bulwark** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You strike an intimidating pose that causes enemies to fear your supposedly heavily armored form. Each foe in a 15-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) who can see you must attempt a DC 22 Will saving throw. On a failure, they’re [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure).

[Sun Sight](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2218)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 122

**Price** 850 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Placed under the eyes like rays of light, this tattoo burns away illusions with the unmerciful brilliance of the sun. You gain a +2 bonus to Perception checks that involve sight. If you're [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7), you receive a new save at the start of each of your turns to end your dazzled condition.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action to Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tattoo casts a 4th-rank [_blazing bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1450), with the rays emitting from your eyes. The number of actions you spend Activating the tattoo determines _blazing bolt’s_ number of rays. The tattoo also attempts to dispel each illusion on a creature hit by a ray ([counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) rank 5th, counteract modifier +19).

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Sun Wheel](/Equipment.aspx?ID=905)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Troubles in Otari</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Troubles in Otari](/Sources.aspx?ID=55) pg. 60

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Created by the priests of a Qadiran sect of [Sarenites](/Deities.aspx?ID=16), the _sun wheels_ were designed to protect the Dawnflower's followers in their quest to hunt down a dangerous cult trying to raise a spawn of the evil god [Rovagug](/Deities.aspx?ID=15). Once they completed their crusade, these priests disbanded and went on to minister other congregations. They each took their _sun wheels_ with them, handing them down to the next generations.

 This copper medallion is etched with a stylized sun, its rays shaped like the spokes of a wagon wheel. It tends to glint brightly when exposed to sunlight. While wearing this pendant, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) checks. You must be good-aligned to use the sun wheel's true power: the following activation, which provides you a shield of burning force.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> concentrate;     **Effect** The _sun wheel_ casts a [_shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=280) spell benefiting you. When you use the spell to prevent damage, you prevent 10 damage instead of 5. If the attacker is adjacent to you, you can choose to deal 2d6 fire damage to it, which it gets a DC 21 basic Reflex save to resist.

 If you choose to deal the fire damage, you can't Activate _the sun wheel_ again until the next morning. If you prevent damage but don't deal the fire damage, you can use it again in 10 minutes, as normal for _shield_.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<traits>

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Bulk** 1

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

This sturdy pole has a rope attached to one end in a loop with the other end extending to the handle. You can pull the handle side of the rope to tighten the loop. Using this loop, you can [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) without having a free hand. A creature grappled this way receives a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls when [Striking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with an unarmed attack. Due to limitations in the size of the loop, a catch pole can only be used on creatures sized Medium or smaller.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 152 **Price** 160 gp **Usage** worn headwear **Bulk** L --- Repurposing and enchanting a helmet worn by a battlefield commander can create a _tactician’s helm_, imparting knowledge of battlefield tactics that feeds off your minor victories. The helm grants you a +1 item bonus to [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) checks. Also, a jewel adorns the brow of the helmet. This jewel becomes charged each time you hit a creature with a [Reactive Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2256). A _tactician’s helm_ can hold up to 2 charges, and its charges reset to 0 when you invest it. **Activate** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))**Cost** 1 charge from the helm; **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You choose one of the following effects.
  • **Charge!** Stride twice.
  • **Move It!** You gain a +2 status bonus to Acrobatics and Athletics checks until the end of this turn.
  • **Protect!** If you're wielding a shield, Stride to a space adjacent to an ally, then Raise your Shield.
  • **Re-Arm!** Interact up to three times. Each of these actions must be used to do something listed under [Interact](/Rules.aspx?ID=2151).

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 57

**Price** 1,250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These stylish shoes were originally created by the Tappin’ Toes Troupe, a group of tap-dancing Taldan bards who achieved massive popularity for their line dance routines. Notoriously lazy when it came to practicing choreography, the troupe enchanted their footwear to enhance their agility. Upon retirement, the troupe sold off their shoe designs, and talented tap shoes have become popular among professional dancers ever since. While wearing the shoes, you gain a +2 item bonus to Acrobatics checks to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369) and [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) an enemy’s space and to Performance checks using dance.

**Activate—Strut Your Stuff** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You click the toes of your _talented tap shoes_ on the ground, and for the next minute, whenever you succeed or critically succeed at a Reflex save to avoid a damaging effect, you can Stride half your Speed as a reaction. However, during this time, you take a –2 item penalty to Stealth checks to [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405).

</column>

    right="Item 10+"

>
[Tales in Timber](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2648)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 202

**Price** 850 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Wooden Breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=36)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Dozens of pictorial stories—told in wood carvings, painting, or pyrography—adorn every outer surface of this _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [wooden breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=36)_. All are old, and many truly ancient, depicting tales set eons ago on the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25). You gain a +2 item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). If you know the [_collective memories_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=15) ritual, you can use Nature instead of [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) if you're the primary caster.

**Activate—Statue Disguise** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The armor makes you look like a wooden statue version of one of the creatures depicted on the armor for 1 hour. This is a 3rd-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159), but it can make you look like any creature depicted on the armor. This doesn't change your size or the capabilities of your body, and it scales the appearance of the creature to match yours. You can Dismiss the activation. This disguise is just real enough to make you somewhat closer to a creature of wood. You're affected by two spells while it lasts: [_oaken resilience_](/Spells.aspx?ID=20) and [_speak with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=294). If you stand still, you gain a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks and DCs to appear as an inanimate wooden statue, in addition to the status bonus to Deception from _illusory disguise_.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Taleteller's Ring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1648)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 161

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn ring

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Smiling faces are inscribed about this silver band. You become a fluent weaver of fictions, gaining a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47), Deception DCs against [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks for storytelling. Whenever you're under suspicion or being questioned by an authority figure, you find yourself compulsively spinning absurd, tall tales that are so unconvincing that they make you look guilty even when you're innocent. The ring's bonuses vanish, and any listener can quickly determine you're lying. Nevertheless, you're completely unable to be honest in such situations.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

Smiling faces are inscribed about this silver band. You become a fluent weaver of fictions, gaining a +2 item bonus to Deception checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=2389), Deception DCs against [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=2302), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks for storytelling. Whenever you're under suspicion or being questioned by an authority figure, you find yourself compulsively spinning absurd, tall tales that are so unconvincing that they make you look guilty even when you're innocent. The ring's bonuses vanish, and any listener can quickly determine you're lying. Nevertheless, you're completely unable to be honest in such situations.

You can attach these light-brown leather flaps adorned with gold stitching to a breastplate or even clothing to protect your upper legs in battle. They give you the freedom to move your body to its limit without worrying about exposing yourself to a hit. </row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

_The Betrayal_ represents selfishness and envy, twisting outcomes toward unfavorable or even devastating results. As long as _The Betrayal_ is invested, you become more adept at hiding who you really are and tricking targets into positions of vulnerability. You gain a +2 item bonus on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks made to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48). This increases to a +3 bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You turn the tables on your foes, bringing one of them into your ranks and compelling them to attack their allies. You cast [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=87) on a creature, but can only issue commands to attack or otherwise harm, betray, or inconvenience its allies. The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 6th level), and the save DC is your class DC.

</column>

_The Big Sky_ represents widespread change or liberation. If you are at least 17th level, the targets also ignore greater difficult terrain.

---

_The Courtesan_ represents political intrigue and social niceties. As long as _The Courtesan_ is invested, you gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You pass the card over your face and become exactly who you need to be; you cast [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159). The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 6th level). You can change your appearance again at any time during the duration by using a three-action activity, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. While under these effects, your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) are one degree of success greater when you use them against a creature that is a lower level than yourself.

May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate **Source** [Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds](/Sources.aspx?ID=203) pg. 73 **Usage** carried --- _The Crows_ represent taking things through violence or force, particularly when done through agility and swiftness rather than brawn. As long as _The Crows_ is invested, you can attempt to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) targets with [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks, and if you're at least trained in [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17), to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) with Thievery checks. When you do so, you gain a +2 item bonus on the attempt, or a +3 item bonus if you're at least 17th level. **Activate** envision, Interact ([teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You hold the card in your hand, and with a flick of the wrist it vanishes, only to be replaced by an object of your choice within 30 feet. The object must be 2 Bulk or less. If that object is unattended, it teleports into your hand automatically. If the object is attended by a creature, you must make a Thievery check against the creature's Reflex DC. **Critical Success** The object teleports into your hand.
**Success** The object vanishes from the target's possession and lands on the ground at a point at a midway point between you two.
**Failure** The object does not vanish, but the creature's grip on it falters and if it doesn't spend an Interact action on its next turn to grip the item, it drops to the ground.
**Critical Failure** You fail to manipulate the object entirely.

fields.text: Item 20 The Crows May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate Unique Artifact Conjuration Invested Magical Source Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds pg. 73 Usage carried The Crows represent taking things through violence or force, particularly when done through agility and swiftness rather than brawn. As long as The Crows is invested, you can attempt to Grapple targets with Acrobatics checks, and if you're at least trained in Thievery, to Disarm with Thievery checks. When you do so, you gain a +2 item bonus on the attempt, or a +3 item bonus if you're at least 17th level. Activate Free Action envision, Interact (teleportation) Frequency once per day; Effect You hold the card in your hand, and with a flick of the wrist it vanishes, only to be replaced by an object of your choice within 30 feet. The object must be 2 Bulk or less. If that object is unattended, it teleports into your hand automatically. If the object is attended by a creature, you must make a Thievery check against the creature's Reflex DC. Critical Success The object teleports into your hand. Success The object vanishes from the target's possession and lands on the ground at a point at a midway point between you two. Failure The object does not vanish, but the creature's grip on it falters and if it doesn't spend an Interact action on its next turn to grip the item, it drops to the ground. Critical Failure You fail to manipulate the object entirely.

[The Cyclone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2503)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** carried

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_The Cyclone_ represents tumultuous evil plots. As long as it is invested, _The Cyclone_ bolsters you with helpful winds that grant you a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks made to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36), [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37), and [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_whirlwind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1033). You do not treat the squares in the _whirlwind_ as difficult terrain, but all other creatures do. The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 8th level), and the save DC is your class DC.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

_The Dance_ represents the delicately balanced rhythms of the universe and the ability stay in step with existence. As long as _The Dance_ is invested, you gain a +2 item bonus on [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You are about to roll initiative;  **Effect** Your body begins to move with anticipation, creating a trail of afterimages for a moment. You can roll initiative with a Performance check. Regardless of what skill you use to roll for initiative, roll the check three times and take the result of your choice. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #191: The Destiny War](/Sources.aspx?ID=199) pg. 73

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** carried

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_The Demon's Lantern_ represents trickery and feats of legerdemain. As long as you have _The Demon's Lantern_ invested, you gain a +2 item bonus to checks made to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61), [Palm an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=67), or [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature hits you with a melee attack;  **Effect** You release a flash of lights and attempt a Reflex saving throw. If your saving throw is higher than the attack roll for the triggering attack, it misses. If the attack misses, the attacker is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) until the end of your next turn.

</column>

>
[The Eclipse](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2538)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds](/Sources.aspx?ID=203) pg. 74

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** carried

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_The Eclipse_ represents self-doubt and loss of purpose, as well as a loss of faith. As long as _The Eclipse_ is invested, you gain a +2 item bonus on [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) checks. This increases to a +3 bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision ([mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A foe that you're aware of and who is within 60 feet achieves a critical success on a saving throw or a Strike;  **Effect** You produce an aura of doubt that overwhelms all foes in a 30-foot emanation and reduces [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in that area to [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408), as if the region were under an eclipse. The triggering creature's critical success is reduced to a regular success. All further saving throws or Strikes attempted by enemies within the emanation suffer a –2 item penalty; saving throws or Strikes attempted by the triggering enemy suffer a –3 penalty instead. You can sustain this aura of doubt for up to 1 minute.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate **Source** [Pathfinder #190: The Choosing](/Sources.aspx?ID=198) pg. 77, [Stolen Fate Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=197) pg. 5 **Usage** carried --- _The Empty Throne_ represents great loss and wisdom from those who are now gone. As long as you have _The Empty Throne_ invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) and [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks made to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) regarding individuals who are no longer alive (such as checks to learn about Taldor's historical founder, but not to learn about its current empress). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level. **Activate** envision; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You overwhelm a target you can see within 60 feet with feelings of helplessness and loss. The creature must attempt a Will DC equal to your class DC. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target can't benefit from circumstance or status bonuses for 1 round.
**Failure** The target can't benefit from circumstance or status bonuses for 1 day, and the target's allies are unable to benefit from circumstance or status bonuses while within 15 feet of the target.
**Critical Failure** As failure, except the duration is 1 week.

_The Fiend_ represents the inevitability of great calamities and pervasive dangers. As long as you have _The Fiend_ invested, when you repeat a non-Strike action you previously took in the same round, you gain a +2 item bonus to checks to perform that action. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You wave the card to create a vision of destruction around you; you cast [_phantasmal calamity_](/Spells.aspx?ID=218), except the area is a 20-foot emanation. The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 6th level), and the save DC is your class DC. You are immune to the effects of your own _phantasmal calamity_.

_The Inquisitor_ represents the search for the truth and the power to see through lies. As long as you have _The Inquisitor_ invested, the results of your Perception Checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85) against targets that are equal to or lower than your level are increased by one degree of success. Against targets that are higher level than you, you instead gain a +2 item bonus to your check. This bonus increases to +3 if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact ([linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You swipe the card over the head of an adjacent creature to delve into their thoughts. You cast [_mind probe_](/Spells.aspx?ID=193), but as a two-action spell rather than one that takes 1 minute to cast. The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 5th level), and the save DC is your class DC.

_The Liar_ represents obsession or treacherous love. As long as you have _The Liar_ invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you're at least 17th level. If the implausibility of your lies prompts a circumstance penalty to your Deception checks or an increase to your Deception DC, reduce that penalty or increase by half.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You touch a weapon and instill faithlessness within it. If you're at least 17th level, you can instead use this activation on a weapon within 30 feet. If the weapon is carried by a creature, it can resist the effect with a successful Will save against your class DC.

As long as you and the target are on the same plane of existence and are both alive, you each remain aware of the other's state—you know the other's direction from you, distance from you, and any conditions affecting them. _The Rakshasa_ represents domination of others to support your own schemes. When you invest _The Rakshasa_, identify a single willing creature within 30 feet as your pledged follower. If you're at least 15th level, you can have up to two pledged followers at once. At 18th level, you can have up to three pledged followers. If you have the maximum pledged followers active and select a new one, a previous pledged follower of your choice is no longer your pledged follower. If this loss kills your pledged follower, you also gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level. The pledged follower is temporarily immune to this activation for 24 hours.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Harrow Court" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=496" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #190: The Choosing](/Sources.aspx?ID=198) pg. 81

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** carried

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

_The Snakebite_ represents poison, assassination, and disharmony. As long as you have _The Snakebite_ invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) and [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks you make for initiative. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you're at least 17th level. The DCs of your [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) effects have a +1 item bonus to targets that are [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) to you when you afflict the target with the poison (the DC retains this bonus for the target's subsequent saves against the affliction, even if the target is no longer flat-footed to you).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_purple worm sting_](/Spells.aspx?ID=242) on a creature within your reach, with a DC equal to your class DC.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** carried

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_The Trader_ represents trades and exchanges of information. As long as you have _The Trader_ invested, you gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks made to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** _The Trader_ allows you to make an exchange with yourself. Press the card to your brow, and then select two skills. Your proficiency rank with those two skills swaps for 1 hour. For example, if you were a master in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) and untrained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), you would become untrained in Athletics and a master in Crafting. If making this swap would break prerequisites to feats, you lose access to those feats until your skill proficiencies change back in an hour.

---

_The Trumpet_ represents timely warning. As long as you have _The Trumpet_ invested, you (and only you) hear the sound of trumpets when you're about to be attacked. This grants you a +2 item bonus to initiative checks made with hearing-based Perception checks. This bonus increases to +3 if you're at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** A blast of inspiring noise erupts from the card in a 60-foot cone. Creatures in the area take 14d6 sonic damage (with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save equal to your class DC). Creatures that fail the save are [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure). The damage increases to 16d6 if you're at least 13th level, to 18d6 if you're at least 15th level, to 20d6 if you're at least 17th level, and to 22d6 if you're at least 19th level.

Creatures in the area take 14d6 sonic damage (with a basic Fortitude save equal to your class DC). Creatures that fail the save are deafened for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure). The damage increases to 16d6 if you're at least 13th level, to 18d6 if you're at least 15th level, to 20d6 if you're at least 17th level, and to 22d6 if you're at least 19th level.

[The Unicorn](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2547)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds](/Sources.aspx?ID=203) pg. 78

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** carried

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_The Unicorn_ represents finding what one seeks. As long as you have _The Unicorn_ invested, you gain a +2 item bonus on Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you're at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You pass _The Unicorn_ across an adjacent closed container and then open the container. Inside, you'll find a Common [consumable](/Traits.aspx?ID=36) alchemical or magic item you need to solve a problem or deal with a situation close at hand. For example, if you're badly wounded, you might find a [_greater healing potion_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=186). If you've been poisoned, you could discover a [_panacea_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=188). If you're faced with a written clue in a language you don't understand, the container might hold a [comprehension elixir](/Equipment.aspx?ID=88). The GM always decides what consumable item is discovered, and it must be equal to or lower than your level. If the consumable isn't used within 1 minute of being discovered, the item vanishes. If there's no appropriate item to solve your situation, the GM can rule that no object is found; in this case, the daily use of _The Unicorn_ is not expended.

_The Vision_ represents arcane knowledge. As long as you have _The Vision_ invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to all checks made to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** A visible bolt of blue energy bursts from your head. Attempt to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about a subject, rolling the check with the most appropriate [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill check. This check always resolves as if you were master in the most appropriate Lore skill to Recall Knowledge on the subject (or if you're at least 15th level, as if you were legendary in that Lore skill). If you're already master (or legendary) in that Lore, the result of your Recall Knowledge check is one degree of success better than it would otherwise be.

<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

---

Developed and widely used by students at the Kitharodian Academy in Oppara, the theatrical mutagen stimulates the creative centers of your brain. This causes your movements to become exaggerated and your voice to become clear. However, the erratic surges of inspiration overload your senses, making it difficult to focus on mundane tasks.

 **Benefit** You gain the listed item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks, and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks. If you're untrained in any of these skills, your proficiency bonus is equal to your level instead of +0. You also gain the listed status bonus to your Speed.

 **Drawback** You take a –1 penalty to Perception checks and Will saves. After any round where you don't spend at least 1 action to Interact with an object, [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=59), Step, or Stride, you're [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of your next turn.

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 616 **Price** 40,000 gp **Usage** worn --- When invested, this ornate crown and its incandescent gemstone meld into your head and take the form of a tattoo. This grants you otherworldly sight and allows you to read auras. No one but you can manipulate the _third eye_ while it’s invested by you. Your heightened senses and ability to sense emotional auras grant you a +3 item bonus to Perception checks.
You continuously see magic auras, as a 9th-level [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) spell, except you see the location of all auras within 30 feet, not just the strongest. If you use a Seek action to study a creature you can see, you can perceive an aura that conveys knowledge of that creature’s health, including all conditions and afflictions it has and an approximate percentage of its remaining Hit Points. **Activate** envision, command; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You gain the effects of an 8th-level [_true seeing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=344) spell.

>
[Thousand-Blade Thesis](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1081)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=67" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 191

**Price** 600 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This collection of lacquered rice paper scrolls mounted on flexible bamboo contains a wealth of calligraphic essays and paintings on the art of war, specifically focused on the use of various weapons in warfare and how to tactically deploy warriors using those weapons to the best possible advantage. Consulting the thesis grants a +2 item bonus to [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks. Like most scholarly compendiums, this usage requires holding the thesis in one hand.

 The thesis also serves as an extradimensional armory for weapons and ammunition. The thesis has a capacity of 5 Bulk, and only weapons and ammunition can be stored within it. You and others can Interact with the thesis to store or retrieve a weapon or piece of ammunition in it, like a mundane container.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _thousand-blade thesis_ dramatically unfurls, and the weapons contained within it spring forth and array themselves impressively in the air, floating within easy reach. For 1 minute, you can use a free action to Interact to draw one of the floating weapons. Others can attempt to nab them out of the air, but to do so they must critically succeed at a [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) check. You can't place weapons back into the thesis until the minute elapses.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Tideplate](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2810)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 231

**Price** 1,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 4
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Full Plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=50)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Rippling water motifs decorate this simple suit of _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=13)_. The plate has been altered for underwater use, so it's check penalty doesn't apply to Acrobatics or Athletics checks in water or similar liquids. While wearing the armor, you gain a +2 item bonus to Athletics checks to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39), and you can breathe underwater. 

**Activate—Ride the Waves** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The ripples on the armor begin to undulate, matching the movement of any nearby water. The armor casts [_water walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=371) on you. 

**Activate—Submerge** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127))
 **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You merge with the water for 10 minutes. While merged, you can't move, you can see through the water if it's clear enough, and you can hear what's going on outside of the water. Water typically can't take damage, but if the water you're merged in is subject to electricity damage or an ability or effect that destroys or dries water, you're expelled from the water and take 10d6 damage. fields.text: Item 10 Tideplate Invested Magical Source GM Core pg. 231 Price 1,000 gp Usage worn armor Bulk 4 Base Armor Full Plate Rippling water motifs decorate this simple suit of +1 resilient full plate . The plate has been altered for underwater use, so it's check penalty doesn't apply to Acrobatics or Athletics checks in water or similar liquids. While wearing the armor, you gain a +2 item bonus to Athletics checks to Swim, and you can breathe underwater. Activate—Ride the Waves Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per hour; Effect The ripples on the armor begin to undulate, matching the movement of any nearby water. The armor casts water walk on you. Activate—Submerge Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate, polymorph) Frequency once per day; Effect You merge with the water for 10 minutes. While merged, you can't move, you can see through the water if it's clear enough, and you can hear what's going on outside of the water. Water typically can't take damage, but if the water you're merged in is subject to electricity damage or an ability or effect that destroys or dries water, you're expelled from the water and take 10d6 damage. Control water expels you without dealing damage.

---

This portable silver anvil has a narrow hoop on one end, through which a long, sturdy chain has been strung. _[Torag's](/Deities.aspx?ID=18) Silver Anvil_ can be wielded as a _+3 [holy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=299) [greater flaming](/Equipment.aspx?ID=295) [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379) [meteor hammer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=97)_. Outside of combat, the anvil can be used with a hammer as an incredibly effective portable forge, heating up the metal to be forged without a furnace and granting a +3 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks involving metalworking. When you use the anvil to successfully [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) a metal item, the item recovers an additional 10 Hit Points (or an additional 20 on a critical success).

</title>

**Price** 33 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Rows of triangles symbolizing shark teeth protect you from danger and enable you to take fierce retaliation against those who try to harm you. Seafarers, especially those on the seas of Minata, wear these tattoos in patterns, with multiple rows of regular triangles. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to navigate bodies of water.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would be hit by an attack against your AC;  **Effect** You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC against the attack, or a +2 circumstance bonus if the attacker is in water or has the [amphibious](/Traits.aspx?ID=207), [aquatic](/Traits.aspx?ID=168), or [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait. Whether the attack hits or misses, you gain a +2 status bonus to damage with the next Strike you make against the attacker before the end of your next turn.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This suit of _+1 [hide armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=7)_ is sickly green and covered in thick warts and nodules, fashioned from the hide of a [trollhound](/Monsters.aspx?ID=835) and imbued with some of the beast's vitality. Wearing this armor gives you a –1 circumstance penalty to all checks made using [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) to interact with [trolls](/Monsters.aspx?ID=395) and a +1 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks used to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) in communities traditionally plagued by troll attacks.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))  **Trigger** You take damage from a melee attack while you have half or fewer of your normal maximum Hit Points;  **Effect** Your body knits itself back together, healing you for 3d8 Hit Points.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the hides of at least two [trollhounds](/Monsters.aspx?ID=835).

---

This jaunty cap can take the form and color of any type of hat you wish upon investing the item, but it always has a peacock feather jutting out from one side. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks while wearing the cap. When you invest the cap, you either increase your Charisma modifer by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You cast [_hypnotize_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1564) (DC 37).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Picking the feather from your cap, you throw it toward a target, casting [_prismatic spray_](/Spells.aspx?ID=233) (DC 35).

<title

[Endless Grimoire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5127)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Grimoire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=387" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 229

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When opened, this grimoire has unlimited pages that, oddly, seem almost eager to transcribe spells. Unlike most grimoires, it has no limits to its number of spells. The grimoire’s eagerness to contain your spells grants you a +1 item bonus to checks to [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366) if you do so by transcribing the spell into the grimoire. If you use the grimoire during your daily preparations and are capable of preparing spells of the appropriate rank, the grimoire’s nature leaks into your mind, allowing you to prepare an additional 1st-rank spell.

---

This sparkling purple belt was made for the youngest member of a family of jugglers and tumblers who traveled with the Crascondo Company. The thought was this would allow the child to safely participate with their elder siblings and cousins, but the belt found itself being “loaned” more and more often to dare-taking elders in the troupe. The _tumbler’s belt_ grants a +2 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks, and whenever you critically succeed at a check to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370), you gain a +10-foot item bonus to your [Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2894) until the end of your turn. While wearing the _tumbler’s belt_, you’re not [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) while you [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369).

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Land With Grace;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You're falling;  **Effect** Treat your fall as if it were 120 feet shorter. Regardless of whether you take damage or not from the fall, you land on your feet.
